content: 1. Ustekinumab is indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in patients who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy. For patients weighing ≤100 kg, the recommended dose is 45 mg subcutaneously at weeks 0 and 4, followed by every 12 weeks thereafter. For patients weighing >100 kg, the dose is increased to 90 mg subcutaneously at the same intervals. 2. Ustekinumab is also indicated for adults with active psoriatic arthritis, either as monotherapy or in combination with methotrexate. The dosing regimen is 45 mg subcutaneously at weeks 0 and 4, followed by every 12 weeks. For patients with co-existing moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and weighing >100 kg, the dose should be increased to 90 mg subcutaneously at the same intervals. 3. Ustekinumab is approved for the treatment of moderately to severely active Crohn's disease in adults. 4. Ustekinumab is indicated for the treatment of moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in adults. 5. The safety and efficacy of ustekinumab in patients with renal or hepatic impairment have not been established. 6. Ustekinumab is approved for the treatment of children aged 6 years and older with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy. Its safety and efficacy in children under 6 years of age have not been established. 7. Ustekinumab is indicated for the treatment of active psoriatic arthritis in children aged 6 years and older. Its safety and efficacy in children under 6 years of age have not been established. 8. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of live vaccines, such as adenovirus types 4 and 7 oral vaccines, through pharmacodynamic antagonism. These vaccines are contraindicated during ustekinumab therapy. Patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations as recommended by current guidelines prior to initiating therapy. Immunosuppressants, including ustekinumab, increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 9. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the influenza virus vaccine (quadrivalent, adjuvanted or intranasal) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. These vaccines are contraindicated during ustekinumab therapy. Patients should be immunized appropriately before starting treatment. 10. Ustekinumab diminishes the effects of the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) live vaccine, as well as the varicella live vaccine, through pharmacodynamic antagonism. These vaccines are contraindicated during ustekinumab therapy. Patients should receive all recommended immunizations prior to treatment initiation. 11. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the rotavirus oral live vaccine and the smallpox/mpox (vaccinia) live vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. These vaccines are contraindicated during ustekinumab therapy. Patients should be immunized according to guidelines before starting treatment. 12. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the yellow fever live vaccine and the zoster live vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. These vaccines are contraindicated during ustekinumab therapy. Patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations before initiating treatment. 13. Ustekinumab diminishes the effects of the Japanese encephalitis virus vaccine and the tick-borne encephalitis vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. These vaccines are contraindicated during ustekinumab therapy. Patients should be immunized appropriately before starting treatment. 14. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the diphtheria and tetanus toxoids, as well as the diphtheria, tetanus, and acellular pertussis vaccine, through pharmacodynamic antagonism. These vaccines are contraindicated during ustekinumab therapy. Patients should receive all recommended immunizations prior to treatment initiation. 15. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis B vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This vaccine is contraindicated during ustekinumab therapy. Patients should be immunized according to guidelines before starting treatment. 16. Ustekinumab diminishes the effects of the anthrax vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This vaccine is contraindicated during ustekinumab therapy. Patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations before initiating treatment. 17. Ustekinumab interacts with various immunosuppressive agents, such as adalimumab, alefacept, anakinra, azathioprine, basiliximab, cyclosporine, etanercept, everolimus, glatiramer, golimumab, hydroxychloroquine sulfate, infliximab, leflunomide, mycophenolate, sirolimus, tacrolimus, and temsirolimus. These combinations increase immunosuppressive effects and the risk of infection. It is recommended to avoid these combinations or use alternative drugs. 18. Ustekinumab interacts with CAR-T cell therapies, such as axicabtagene ciloleucel, brexucabtagene autoleucel, ciltacabtagene autoleucel, idecabtagene vicleucel, and lisocabtagene maraleucel. These combinations increase immunosuppressive effects and the risk of infection. It is recommended to avoid these combinations or use alternative drugs. 19. Live-attenuated vaccines should be avoided for at least three months after discontinuing immunosuppressive therapy, including ustekinumab, due to the increased risk of infection. 20. Ustekinumab decreases the effects of the measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella (MMRV) live vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This vaccine is contraindicated during ustekinumab therapy. Patients should receive all recommended immunizations prior to treatment initiation.
